- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after positive sentiment spikes.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often holds high values; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 periods ahead.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated oscillations (e.g., +0.3, -0.4, +0.3), model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% volatility in forecast for next 3–5 days.
